title: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah jemput orang ramai ke ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ sempena perkahwinan
body: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah jemput orang ramai ke ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ sempena perkahwinan KUALA LUMPUR – Bakal raja sehari, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan tunangnya, Bella Astillah menjemput orang ramai menghadiri majlis ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ sempena perkahwinan mereka yang bakal berlangsung pada 10 Oktober ini. Majlis berkenaan akan diadakan di Muar, Johor pada 25 Oktober, sebelum diteruskan di Kota Kinabalu, Sabah pada 31 Oktober. Syed Saddiq yang juga Ahli Parlimen Muar berkata, kedua-dua majlis resepsi itu dirancang dalam tempoh kurang dua bulan, sekali gus menyebabkan mereka berdepan kekangan masa dan kesukaran mendapatkan lokasi yang sesuai. Katanya, konsep ‘Kenduri Rakyat’ dipilih dengan mengetengahkan semangat rewang dan meraikan perkahwinan bersama masyarakat. “Majlis kahwin kami nanti bertemakan rewang. Kalau sebelum ini, sambutan Hari Raya yang saya anjurkan di Muar sudah mencecah 10,000 orang, jadi kita jangka untuk kenduri kami lebih ramai yang akan datang. “Jadi, majlis itu nanti berkonsepkan ‘siapa cepat dia dapat’ (nikmati juadah). Jika makanan habis sekalipun, kami akan berada di sana untuk bersama dengan tetamu,” katanya pada majlis Walimatulurus Bella Astillah dan Syed Saddiq, di sini hari ini. Sebanyak 10,000 cenderahati istimewa turut disediakan untuk tetamu yang hadir ke majlis berkenaan. Ditanya mengenai perasaannya menghitung hari bahagia bersama Bella pada 10 Oktober nanti, Syed Saddiq pantas menjawab: “Saya tak sabar nak menghalalkan hubungan kami.” Menurut Syed Saddiq, dia mengakui tidak rasa berdebar, tetapi tidak sabar untuk bergelar suami kepada Bella. “Perasaan saya lebih kepada tidak sabar berbanding berdebar. Tak sabar nak kongsikan hari bahagia kami bersama semua termasuklah keluarga dan sahabat andai. “Saya selalu kongsikan kepada bakal isteri saya, kebahagiaan perlu dikongsikan kepada semua kerana tanpa doa, sokongan dan dorongan orang ramai, mungkin hari ini (perkahwinan) tidak akan terjadi. Setiap orang ada saham dalam menjayakan perkahwinan kami,” katanya. Sebelum ini, Syed Saddiq dan Bella mengesahkan mereka bakal disatukan sebagai suami isteri pada 10 Oktober ini. Majlis pernikahan pasangan itu dijadual berlangsung di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank, di sini, dengan konsep serba putih yang disulami elemen Arab dan Islamik atas permintaan keluarga. Menariknya perjalanan kisah cinta mereka dari mula perkenalan sehingga menjelang hari perkahwinan bakal disiarkan dalam program khas Walimatulurus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq yang akan ditayangkan di Astro Ria bermula 6 Oktober 2026. Syed Saddiq dan Bella dilaporkan mula berkenalan dengan lebih rapat pada 2025 sebelum mengikat tali pertunangan pada 28 Mac lalu.

title: '[VIDEO] ‘Baru Hendak Tulis Muka Surat Pertama’ – Syed Saddiq & Bella Astillah Akui Tak Layak Disamakan Dengan Tun M & Allahyarhamah Tun Hasmah
body: 'Ahli Parlimen Muar, Syed Saddiq dan bakal isterinya, Bella Astillah tidak bersetuju dengan kenyataan yang menyamakan kisah cinta mereka dengan pasangan negarawan, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad dan Allahyarhamah Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali. Artikel Berkaitan: Bella Astillah Kongsi Keadaan Syed Saddiq – ‘Dia Tak Mampu Teruskan Apa Yang Telah Dirancang Hari Ini’ Artikel Berkaitan: [VIDEO] ‘Berdebar? Tidak, Saya Gembira’ – Syed Saddiq Tak layak disamakan Dalam satu sesi temu bual, Saddiq menegaskan perbandingan itu terlalu jauh, malah merasakan mereka tidak layak apabila persamaan tersebut dibuat. Saya rasa kami tidak layak untuk dibandingkan dengan Allahyarhamah dan juga Tun Dr. Mahathir. Tidak dekat pun, malah tidak sampai satu peratus kerana kalau kita lihat jasa mereka, ia memang luar biasa. Saddiq berkata demikian pada sidang media Walimatulurus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq di Kuala Lumpur pada Jumaat. Mengulas lebih lanjut, Saddiq berkata Allahyarhamah Tun Dr Siti Hasmah merupakan tokoh yang wajar dicontohi khususnya dalam bidang perubatan. Tun Dr Siti Hasmah salah seorang doktor wanita terawal yang memberikan inspirasi kepada wanita. Beliau satu-satunya doktor wanita dalam kelompoknya ketika itu di Singapura dan mendapat biasiswa. Bila pulang untuk berkhidmat, pada awalnya beliau berada di kota, tetapi apabila diberikan ujian dan cabaran untuk dihantar ke kawasan luar bandar, beliau tidak mengeluh. Beliau pergi membantu dan mendidik keluarga serta anak-anak di sana untuk menerima pendidikan moden. Beliau adalah antara yang terawal dan perintis. Sementara itu, Saddiq menyifatkan Tun Mahathir sebagai tokoh yang banyak memberi sumbangan kepada negara. Tun Dr Mahathir lagilah. Saya rasa saya tidak perlu menyenaraikan satu per satu pencapaian dan jasa beliau kepada negara yang sehingga hari ini kita masih menerima manfaatnya. Jadi, sejujurnya, bagi mereka yang berkongsikan perkara ini, saya tahu ia datang daripada niat yang baik. Tetapi jawapan kami, kita tidak layak untuk disamakan kerana mereka jauh lebih ke hadapan daripada kami. Kata Saddiq, kisah percintaan mereka juga tidak setara untuk disamakan dengan pasangan negarawan itu memandangkan ikatan hubungan mereka sedang dibina dan masih berada di peringkat awal. Saya tahu mungkin ada yang kata, ‘Oh, tetapi bukan daripada sudut sumbangan kepada negara, mungkin daripada sudut cinta.’ Itu pun saya rasa kami tidak layak. Kerana kami ini baru hendak berkahwin, hendak menghalalkan hubungan. Mereka ini sudah 70 tahun meraikan cinta dan kebijaksanaan bersama. Kami belum sampai pun 25 tahun, baru hendak membuka bab atau buku yang pertama. Kalau kita ibaratkan seperti sebuah buku, kami baru hendak menulis muka surat pertama. Mereka bukan sekadar menulis muka surat pertama, mungkin mereka sudah mempunyai perpustakaan sendiri yang boleh berkongsikan kisah cinta mereka. Bukan satu buku, tetapi sudah beribu-ribu buku. Dalam perkembangan lain, Saddiq dan Bella akan disatukan sebagai suami isteri pada sebuah majlis di Kuala Lumpur pada 10 Oktober depan. Majlis pernikahan mereka akan berlangsung di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank dengan konsep serba putih disulami elemen Arab atau Islamik atas permintaan keluarga. title: 'F1 Singapore Grand Prix value proposition still strong after 18 years
body: 'SINGAPORE – For 18 years, Singapore has marketed its Formula 1 Grand Prix not just as a motor race, but as a showcase of what the Lion City can do when it turns several kilometres of floodlit roads along the waterfront at dusk into a global stage.  Since September 2008, the Marina Bay Street Circuit has become one of the most iconic events on the F1 calendar, offering something no other city did – the first-ever night race.  The spectacle helped establish Singapore as a distinctive stop on the F1 calendar, while giving the city-state a high-profile platform to promote its hospitality industry, infrastructure, business environment and ability to stage a complex international event.  Now, a few countries in the region are seeking to replicate Singapore’s success and join the F1 bandwagon in hopes of global attention and attracting high-spending visitors.  After a nine-year hiatus, Malaysia is set to host an F1 race in Sepang again in October, while Thailand is targeting a street race in Bangkok’s Chatuchak area as early as 2028.  The emergence of new Asian contenders raises questions about whether the Singapore Grand Prix can continue to distinguish itself or if fans will be drawn away to rival races.  Market observers and economists believe it can.  “F1 is still delivering benefits to Singapore that outweigh the cost of hosting the event,” said Brian Lee, an economist at Maybank.  “While the direct tourism benefits may face diminishing returns, the race remains valuable as a platform for attracting high-spending visitors, business events and global capital,” he added.  He noted that the 2025 F1 race weekend drew a sell-out crowd of more than 300,000 fans. That was the second-highest attendance in the event’s history and an almost 12 per cent jump from 2024, suggesting the novelty remained.  Guy Llewellyn, academic director for Asia-Pacific at EHL Hospitality Business School, said it would be hard for other cities to replicate Singapore’s experience after it has run the event for 18 years, coordinating different stakeholders and building a strong international reputation.  “Singapore’s strategy has gradually evolved from hosting a sporting event to hosting a citywide festival. The concerts, entertainment zones, dining experiences, and new Barge Stage programming mean that visitors can spend an entire day in Marina Bay without focusing exclusively on racing,” the assistant professor said.  The Barge Stage waterfront amphitheatre will be unveiled in 2026 along with a line-up of international DJs.  “Few destinations can offer a Formula 1 circuit, internationally branded hotels, fine dining, nightlife and entertainment venues all within walking distance of one another,” Llewellyn said.  However, while being the first night race was once a powerful differentiator, the novelty naturally fades over time, making the broader ecosystem increasingly important in setting the experience apart, he added.  Faizal Yahya, senior research fellow at the Institute of Policy Studies at NUS’ Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, also believes the race should go on.  The returns have been “a massive net positive”, as Singapore has gained a lot economically, strategically, and in terms of its global image, Yahya said.  From the inaugural night race in 2008 until 2024, the event generated around $2.2 billion in incremental tourism receipts, mostly for accommodation, attraction tickets, food and beverage, shopping and airfares. It also attracted more than 720,000 visitors over the period.  Lee said that this is equivalent to $129 million a year in incremental spending from tourists attending the race. That is 0.4 per cent of Singapore’s 2025 aggregate tourism receipts.  While this may be close to the $140 million annual cost of organising the race, there are other beneficiaries that are not captured by the tourism receipt figures.  These include companies involved in the track and venue setup, advertising and others that support the event, ranging from raw material suppliers, equipment rental, logistics and even laundry and cleaning services, Lee said.  Beyond grandstand ticket sales, F1’s ripple effect extends to drawing other high-profile events around the race period.  Every year, about 25 to 30 international conferences – including the Forbes Global CEO Conference, the Milken Institute Asia Summit and TOKEN2049 – have been held around race week, bringing in around 90,000 C-suites to Singapore.  High-net-worth travellers, who make up 30 per cent of F1 visitors, account for 40 per cent of tourist spending during race week, pushing up occupancy rates and hotel room rates even outside the race vicinity.  A large share of the race’s contracts is subcontracted to Singapore-based small and medium-sized enterprises, including firms in engineering, construction and hospitality, the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) said.  About 30,000 staff, contractors and stakeholders work on each race. More than 1,000 students from the Institute of Technical Education and polytechnics are also trained each year for roles around the circuit, giving them exposure to the organisation of a major international event.  “This creates temporary employment for over 30,000 workers and students across logistics, advanced engineering, hospitality and specialised event staging,” Yahya said.  With millions of people around the world watching the Singapore race on television and online, the event is a global advertisement for the Republic, showcasing its infrastructure, safety, business environment and city life, he added.  The 2019 Singapore Grand Prix was estimated to have generated $70 million to $75 million in media value, according to a McKinsey study cited by METI.  Maintaining the head start  In 2026, Singapore will host its first-ever F1 Sprint race, on Saturday, Oct 10 – a two-day, 100km race that is hosted by just six circuits this season.  The Sprint format alters the dynamic of the traditional Marina Bay Street Circuit weekend, and could make the Singapore race weekend feel like two big race days instead of one, said Llewellyn.  Saturday gets its own race, giving fans another reason to come earlier and stay longer.  For hotels, it offers an opportunity to earn more if more guests arrive on Thursday and stay longer.  It remains to be seen whether fans will see the Sprint as a must-attend event, since this is Singapore’s first time hosting a Sprint, Llewellyn said.  To keep its competitive edge, experts said Singapore must continue to convert more F1 race visitors into long-term tourists and business connections by linking race week with high-value conferences, business-cum-leisure packages, and MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, and exhibitions) events.  Regional travel partnerships can encourage onward trips across ASEAN, while digital matchmaking connects delegates with local businesses. Hosting networking events in Marina Bay and Orchard Road can further showcase Singapore’s commercial ecosystem.  The Singapore Grand Prix was never just a sporting event from the start. It is being used as a tourism draw, a business-networking platform, a showcase for local companies and a recurring global advertisement for the city.  “The issue is less about whether Singapore should continue hosting F1, and more about whether it can continue extracting scarcity value from the event as competing cities replicate the street-race model,” Lee said.

title: 'Batu Kawan’s Takeover of MKH Crosses 95%
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 30): Batu Kawan Bhd’s (KL:BKAWAN) unconditional mandatory takeover of MKH Bhd (KL:MKH) has crossed the 95% threshold, paving the way for the property developer’s delisting. As at market close on Wednesday, Batu Kawan and its wholly owned unit Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd, together with parties acting in concert, held 548.85 million MKH shares, representing a 95.16% stake, according to a statement issued on their behalf by Maybank Investment Bank Bhd. With the offeror having received valid acceptances of not less than nine-tenths in the nominal value of the offer shares, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will invoke Section 222(1) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 to compulsorily acquire the remaining MKH shares from dissenting shareholders, the statement said. The takeover offer, it said, will remain open until Oct 8, following an extension from the original Sept 17 closing date. Bursa Malaysia Securities will suspend trading of MKH shares upon the expiry of five market days from Oct 8. Thereafter, Batu Kawan and Whitmore will procure MKH to take the necessary steps to withdraw its listing status from Bursa Malaysia. Two weeks ago, minority shareholders of MKH and its separately listed plantation arm, MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd (KL:MKHOP), were given contrasting recommendations regarding Batu Kawan's dual takeover play. Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd, the independent adviser appointed by MKH, deemed the RM2 cash buyout “not fair but reasonable”, noting that the offer price undervalues the property developer’s fair asset worth. On the other hand, Mainstreet Advisers Sdn Bhd urged MKH Oil Palm shareholders to reject the related 66.26 sen per share buyout offer, labelling it "not fair and not reasonable". Mainstreet emphasised that the offer represents a steep 47% discount to MKH Oil Palm's net asset value, and noted that Batu Kawan intends to maintain the plantation unit's listing. The takeover was initiated in May, when Batu Kawan, through Whitmore, agreed to acquire a combined 47.7% stake in MKH from members of the Chen family for RM549.8 million, or RM2 per share. The RM2 offer valued the total cost of taking MKH private at up to RM1.15 billion, including the initial stake purchase. Batu Kawan's share price closed unchanged at RM20.52 on Wednesday, with a market capitalisation of RM8.2 billion. MKH also settled unchanged at RM1.99 with a market value of RM1.17 billion, while MKH Oil Palm closed unchanged at 64.5 sen, valuing the group at RM660 million. title: 'S P Setia Launches 100-acre Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines
body: 'S P Setia Bhd on Monday officially launched Setia Fontaines Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines, Kepala Batas, marking a significant milestone in the group’s continued placemaking and township development efforts in Penang. From left: Penang state executive councillor for tourism and creative economy Wong Hon Wai, Penang state secretary Datuk Dr Jafri Abdul Jalil, Yang di-Pertua Negeri of Penang Tun Ramli Ngah Talib, S P Setia president and CEO Datuk Zaini Yusoff and member of the Penang state legislative assembly Bukhori Ghazali. KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 21): S P Setia Bhd (KL:SPSETIA) officially launched Setia Fontaines Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines in Kepala Batas, Penang — marking a significant milestone in the group's placemaking and township development efforts in Penang. According to a press statement on Monday, the launch was graced by Yang di-Pertua Negeri of Penang Tun Ramli Ngah Talib and his wife Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah, alongside state representatives, government agencies, strategic partners, invited guests, residents and members of the public. Also present was Penang state executive councillor for tourism and creative economy Wong Hon Wai. "This effort not only enhances the value and appeal of Setia Fontaines as a premier township development but also contributes meaningfully to the broader socio-economic growth and development of Kepala Batas and the Northern Seberang Perai region," Wong said. He added that the project reflects the important role private-sector investment plays in creating sustainable communities, strengthening local economies and supporting the state's long-term development aspirations. Set within the wider Setia Fontaines development, the 100-acre Heritage Park incorporates a 63-acre man-made lake and a musical fountain to support quality living, recreation, wellness and community engagement. S P Setia president and CEO Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the launch reflects the group's long-term commitment to Penang and its belief that successful townships must be built around people, community and shared experiences. "Setia Fontaines Heritage Park represents our continued commitment to building beyond homes. Through thoughtful placemaking, green public spaces and community-led experiences, we are shaping Setia Fontaines into an integrated township that contributes to Penang’s growth while creating long-term value for residents, visitors and the wider community," Zaini said. He added that Heritage Park is envisioned as more than a township amenity, serving as a lifestyle and recreational attraction with potential to support visitation, public engagement and destination appeal for Seberang Perai Utara and the wider northern region. The official launch was followed by the Jom Mai Setia Fontaines Carnival, a large-scale community activation featuring family activities, Malaysia Day-themed programmes, cultural and entertainment performances, and tourism-related activations. Strategic collaborations with Tourism Malaysia, Penang Global Tourism and Maybank further supported the destination-branding direction of the programme. Setia Fontaines is planned as an integrated township in Kepala Batas, incorporating residential, commercial, recreational, lifestyle and future employment components within a single development. title: 'KLIA T2 Retail Occupancy Holds Steady Despite Airline Capacity Cuts
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 29): Visitors walking through Kuala Lumpur International Airport's Terminal 2 (KLIA T2) will notice hoardings — temporary boards and barricades put up around shops that are empty or under renovation — at several areas of its retail section. While these appear just as airlines trim flight capacity to counter soaring fuel costs, the boarded-up spaces do not necessarily signal a broader downturn in the terminal's retail performance. Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB), which operates KLIA and 38 other airports in the country, said tenant occupancy at KLIA T2 remained resilient despite a decline in passenger traffic. Commercial occupancy stood at 93% currently, up from 92% a year earlier. “Some of the hoardings currently visible within the terminal are part of a planned reconfiguration of space to improve passenger processing and circulation,” MAHB said in an email response to questions from The Edge Malaysia. The airport operator said some commercial areas were being repurposed for this purpose, with several outlets in the affected areas scheduled to be progressively phased out by the end of the year. MAHB declined to disclose tenant level sales or passenger spending, citing commercial sensitivity. It said commercial performance depended on factors beyond passenger volumes, including passenger profiles, outlet locations, retail categories and the performance of individual businesses. The clarification comes as airlines operating from KLIA T2 contend with a sharp rise in fuel costs and weaker capacity on some routes since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February. Global average jet fuel prices reached US$194.90 per barrel in the week ended Sept 18 — up 116.5% from a year earlier — according to data from Platts and S&P Global. Airlines have been particularly exposed to the increase because fuel typically accounts for between 30% and 50% of their operating costs. Budget carriers such as AirAsia Group Bhd (KL:AAGB) and Batik Air Malaysia, which remain largely unhedged, have been hit by the volatility in the jet fuel market. In response, some airlines have cut capacity by as much as 30% since April to limit fuel consumption and contain costs. AirAsia is the largest airline tenant at KLIA T2. Other carriers operating from the terminal include Scoot, Spring Airlines, Cebu Pacific Airways, Lucky Air, Qingdao Airlines and Shandong Airlines. On Sept 18, AirAsia said it had reduced capacity by 20% to 25% in the third quarter, traditionally a weaker travel period. It expects to restore capacity towards pre-Iran war levels in the fourth quarter, when year-end travel demand typically strengthens. The impact of the capacity cuts have been reflected in KLIA T2's footfall. While total passenger traffic across KLIA rose 2.1% year-on-year to 41.95 million between January and August this year, the headline growth masks a clear divergence between its two terminals. Traffic at Terminal 1 climbed roughly 8% y-o-y to 24.46 million passengers, but T2 saw numbers fall 5% y-o-y to 17.48 million over the same period. Still, MAHB said traffic had begun to recover from June. Total KLIA passenger movements increased from 4.7 million in June to five million in July and 5.2 million in August, with both terminals recording improvements. At T2, passenger numbers rose from 1.83 million in June to 1.86 million in July, and 1.98 million in August. “While T2 traffic remains below the corresponding period in 2025, the recent trend shows a gradual recovery following the capacity reductions experienced during the middle of the year,” MAHB said. The airport operator said it would continue to monitor airline capacity, passenger traffic and commercial performance. It added that the recent recovery in passenger movements provides a more balanced picture of conditions at both KLIA terminals than the weaker traffic figures recorded earlier in the year. For airlines, however, fuel remains a significant pressure point. In a Sept 21 report, Maybank Investment Bank Research estimated that every US$1 increase in the price of jet fuel could reduce AirAsia’s earnings by RM75 million. AirAsia shares closed half a sen or 0.94% lower at 52.5 sen on Monday, valuing the group at RM1.76 billion. The stock has fallen about 70% since the start of the year. title: 'AHB Maintains Five Sen Income Distribution For FY2026
body: 'Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) has maintained its income distribution at five sen per unit for the financial year ended Sept 30, 2026, benefiting more than 82,000 unit holders.  The final distribution for the six months ended Sept 30 was set at 2.1 sen per unit, alongside a 0.4 sen bonus distribution declared by fund sponsor Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB).  Together with the 2.5 sen interim distribution declared in April, the total distribution for FY2026 comes to five sen per unit.  PHB said RM120.13 million will be paid in the final round, bringing the total annual distribution to RM236.41 million.  The bonus distribution applies to the first 1,000,000 units held by each unit holder.  PHB Group Managing Director Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad said the full-year distribution reflected the resilience of AHB and its underlying property portfolio.  “AHB’s performance this year demonstrates our commitment to continue providing competitive returns to unit holders. At the same time, we remain focused on strengthening AHB’s position as an investment instrument of choice for Bumiputera investors through prudent capital management, dynamic investment strategies and continuous portfolio optimisation to ensure sustainable growth and long-term value creation,” he said.  PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM) Chief Executive Officer Zulkifli Ishak said the fund manager would continue managing AHB responsibly to ensure it remained accessible to Bumiputera investors.  The distribution will be paid in the form of AHB units and credited directly into unit holders’ AHB accounts by Oct 13. The units will be automatically reinvested, allowing holders to increase their holdings.  Bumiputera investors can subscribe to AHB at a fixed price of RM1 per unit, with a minimum investment of RM100 and maximum of RM1 million. Subscriptions are available through authorised distributors including Maybank, AmBank, AmBank Islamic, Bank Islam Malaysia and Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia.

title: 'The Ladies 2026: 42 pemain mulakan saingan pusingan pertama - Portal Berita RTM
body: 'SERI KEMBANGAN, 1 Oktober – Pusingan pertama Kejohanan Golf Wanita The Ladies 2026 menyaksikan 42 pemain mula beraksi seawal pukul 7.30 pagi tadi. Saingan kali ini turut menampilkan gandingan pemain profesional serta amatur seperti Allycia Gan, Liyana Durisic, Durriyah Damian dan Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan tersebut adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan. Kejohanan tersebut juga sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi. Penganjuran itu membawa mesej yang jelas kepada generasi muda bahawa kerjaya dalam bidang sukan golf profesional bukan mustahil untuk dicapai oleh wanita Malaysia. Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja di The Mines Resort and Golf Club, kelmarin. Kejohanan tersebut kembali buat kali kedua dengan menyasarkan visi menjadi antara kejohanan wanita berprestij di rantau ini, sebelum melangkah ke pentas antarabangsa. Kejohanan yang berlangsung di Kelab Golf The Mines dari 1 hingga 3 Oktober itu menawarkan jumlah hadiah wang tunai sehingga RM100,000.

title: 'Lelaki bebas tuduhan tipu RM108,500
body: 'Kota Kinabalu: Seorang lelaki bekerja sendiri berusia 50 tahun dilepas dan dibebaskan daripada pertuduhan menipu seorang lelaki membabitkan RM108,500 berkaitan beberapa projek di Kinabatangan dan Semporna. Majistret Wan Farrah Farriza Wan Ghazali memutuskan demikian selepas mendapati pihak pendakwaan gagal membuktikan kes prima facie terhadap Abdillah Hamzah. Abdillah dilepas dan dibebaskan tanpa dipanggil membela diri. Abdillah didakwa menipu Chong Kong Fah dengan memperdayakannya sehingga mempercayai bahawa tertuduh mengurus beberapa projek iaitu pembinaan jalan konkrit ke SMK Bukit Garam, Kinabatangan; menaik taraf sistem perparitan di Taman Perumahan Bukit Permata, Kinabatangan; membaiki jeti terapung di Dataran Lepa-Lepa, Semporna; menaik taraf jalan di kawasan Dolton Town, Semporna; dan membaiki rumah di Semporna. Pertuduhan menyatakan Chong memasukkan wang berkenaan ke dalam akaun syarikat bernama Dilwani Enterprise, yang tidak akan dilakukannya sekiranya tidak diperdayakan sedemikian. Kesalahan itu didakwa dilakukan antara 23 Jun 2016 dan 5 Disember 2018 di Maybank cawangan Semporna. Pertuduhan mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan memperuntukkan hukuman penjara sehingga 10 tahun dan sebatan serta boleh didenda jika sabit kesalahan. Pihak pendakwaan memanggil enam saksi sepanjang perbicaraan. Timbalan Pendakwa Raya (TPR) Noor Hafizah Anggu hadir bagi pihak TPR Arfa Anchal Khan manakala peguam Nurul Rafeeqa Afdul Mutolip mewakili Abdillah. Sementara itu seorang lelaki berusia 64 tahun mengaku bersalah menyebabkan kecederaan parah terhadap seorang lelaki menggunakan parang. Bagaimanapun Hakim Mahkamah Sesyen Marlina Ibrahim menangguhkan hukuman terhadap Paul Akang ke 28 Oktober ini sementara menunggu laporan perubatan dan forensik. Sementara menunggu tarikh berkenaan, Paul direman lanjut. Paul didakwa menyebabkan kecederaan serius terhadap lelaki berusia 45 tahun itu menggunakan senjata berkenaan pada jam 5 petang, 21 September lalu di hadapan sebuah rumah di Kampung Kelansatan, Kuala Penyu. title: 'VS Surprise 4Q Return to Core Profit Prompts Three Brokers to Upgrade
body: 'V.S Industry returned to core profitability in 4QFY26, posting a RM19.5 million core net profit after a RM38.0 million core loss in the previous quarter and a RM31.5 million core loss a year earlier. This narrowed its FY26 core net loss to RM21.5 million, a better-than-expected result. Stronger orders from key brand owners lifted sales and improved operating leverage. Hong Leong Investment Bank analyst Sam Jun Kit upgraded V.S Industry to “Hold” from “Sell” and raised his target price to RM0.23 from RM0.12, implying a 6.1% downside. He expects a healthier earnings run rate in FY27, supported by a potential turnaround in the Philippines and higher production allocations from a key customer to V.S Industry’s Malaysian operations. However, Sam remains cautious on the consumer electronics manufacturing services sector: weak consumer sentiment, uncertain demand beyond the festive-season peak and potential wage pressure could limit further upside. Sam Jun Kit is ranked No.4 among 24 analysts covering the industrial products and services sector on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He holds a 50% expert rating and a 43% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. Meanwhile, Maybank Investment Bank analyst Lucas Sim (42% expert rating) also upgraded the stock to “Hold” from “Sell”, lifting his target price to RM0.25 from RM0.10, implying a 2% upside. Looking ahead, Lucas expects stronger order loadings to support an earnings recovery and raised his FY27E–FY28E forecasts by 41%–58%. He remains cautious about weak consumer demand and rising costs, which could limit the pace of that recovery. Affin Hwang Investment Bank analysts Kevin Low (41% expert rating) and Haziq Haizan (no expert rating) upgraded the stock to “Hold” from “Sell”, lifting their target price to RM0.24 from RM0.14, implying a 2% downside. As of 9:28 a.m. on September 30, V.S Industry's share price rose 4.3% to RM0.245. Disclaimer: All content is AI-aggregated from public sources for informational and educational purposes only. title: 'Maybank’s MAE App Now Checks Your Phone For More Scam Risks
body: 'Maybank has upgraded Malware Shielding, the security check built into its MAE app. According to Maybank’s announcement, the new version is rolling out in stages from 26 September 2026. The upgrade lets it spot more kinds of risk on your phone.  If it finds a risk, MAE will tell you what’s wrong and how to fix it. For more serious risks, it may stop you from using the app until the problem is gone.  Malware Shielding Checks Your Phone Every Time You Open MAE  Malware is harmful software that scammers trick people into installing. They often send a link to an app file instead of pointing people to an official app store. Once malware is on a phone, it can read the TAC or OTP codes your bank sends you, or let a scammer control the phone from far away and approve transfers.  Malware Shielding looks for these dangers each time you launch MAE. In 2024, the Association of Banks in Malaysia (ABM) said this kind of check only runs when you open a banking app. It doesn’t keep running in the background all day. Maybank says the feature doesn’t collect or store the personal content on your phone, such as your photos, messages, or contacts.  The Phone Settings And Apps MAE Now Looks Out For  Some of the risks on Maybank’s list are clearly dangerous, such as scam apps. Others are everyday tools. Maybank says a VPN or a keyboard app from an unknown developer may expose your password, your TAC, or other banking details to people you don’t know.  Several of these have normal uses. People use VPNs for work or to watch shows from other countries, and some use screen recording to show a family member how to pay a bill. Maybank’s list doesn’t make exceptions for these, so switch them off before you open MAE.  A Warning Or A Lockout Depends On The Risk  Malware Shielding may warn you, show you steps to fix the problem, or block MAE until it’s fixed. Maybank’s FAQ says this depends on how serious the risk is.  Maybank doesn’t say which risks only bring up a warning and which lock the app. Because the check runs every time you open MAE, a setting you switch on later, such as screen recording, can still trigger it the next time you log in.  Other banks run similar checks. Members of ABM and the Association of Islamic Banking and Financial Institutions Malaysia (AIBIM) began adding malware shielding to their apps in August 2024. Banks that had switched it on by then included CIMB, Public Bank, RHB, and UOB, so you may see similar warnings in their apps too.  In June 2026, ABM reported that malware shielding helped stop more than 60,000 malware-related scam attempts in 2025, involving about RM22 million in potential losses.  A Malware Shielding Alert Can Affect Whether You Get Your Money Back  Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) SEFT policy sets out when banks compensate victims of unauthorised transactions, including money taken through malware. However, BNM’s 2025 Annual Report says some victims may be held fully responsible and get no compensation at all. One example it gives is a victim who downloads a harmful app even after the bank has warned them about the risk.  So if you tap past a Malware Shielding alert and carry on, it could be harder to get compensation if a scammer later takes money from your account.  Update MAE And Tap Agree To Keep Using It  To get added Malware Shielding protection, update MAE to the latest version from Google Play, the App Store, or Huawei AppGallery. After the update, MAE will ask you to read and agree to the Malware Shielding terms and conditions. This step is compulsory, so you can’t keep using the app until you tap “Agree”.  If MAE blocks you, follow the steps on your screen. You may be asked to delete a suspicious app, turn off a setting such as Developer Mode, stop screen sharing or recording, switch to a supported phone, or reinstall MAE from an official app store. Once that’s done, close MAE and open it again.  If you’re still locked out, call Maybank Group Customer Care on 1-300-88-6688, or +603-7844 3696 from overseas. If you think money has already left your account, turn on your bank’s kill switch and call the National Scam Response Centre on 997. The line is open 24 hours, and your call counts as a police report.

title: 'SAMSUNG MALAYSIA AND MAYBANK PARTNER TO LAUNCH MALAYSIA’S FIRST SAMSUNG WALLET QR PAYMENT EXPERIENCE MalaysianUpdates
body: 'Kuala Lumpur, 24 July 2026 — Samsung Malaysia Electronics (SME) Sdn Bhd (Samsung) and Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) have entered into a strategic partnership to introduce Malaysia’s first Samsung Wallet QR Payment experience, marking a significant development in the country’s digital payments landscape. The collaboration, formalised through the signing of a Collaboration Agreement, combines Samsung’s mobile innovation with Maybank’s established digital banking ecosystem to provide Samsung Galaxy users with a faster, more seamless way to make everyday payments. Beginning 21 July 2026, eligible Samsung Galaxy users will be able to access Maybank’s MAE Scan & Pay functionality directly within Samsung Wallet through the latest application and software updates. As Malaysia continues its transition towards a cashless economy, the partnership reflects both companies’ commitment to making digital payments simpler, more secure and convenient for customers across urban and suburban communities. With QR Payment integrated directly into Samsung Wallet, users can quickly access the feature with a swipe before using Maybank’s Scan & Pay via the MAE app to complete their transactions. The integrated experience is designed to reduce unnecessary steps when making payments, whether users are purchasing meals, groceries, coffee or other everyday essentials. The QR payment functionality can also be used regionally across Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Cambodia, providing greater convenience for Samsung Galaxy users when making payments beyond Malaysia. President of Samsung Malaysia Electronics, Charles Kim, said the partnership with Maybank represents an important step in expanding the Samsung Wallet ecosystem in Malaysia. He added that integrating QR payments directly into Samsung Wallet is intended to make everyday transactions more effortless, allowing users to swipe, scan and pay within seconds. Meanwhile, Mohd Amri Mohd Sofian, Head of Community Financial Services Malaysia at Maybank, said the collaboration supports the Bank’s ROAR30 ambitions by focusing on intuitive digital experiences and frictionless payment journeys. Integrating MAE Scan & Pay directly into Samsung Wallet, he said, provides customers with greater convenience while maintaining the security and reliability associated with Maybank’s digital banking services. Beyond convenience, users can also earn Samsung Reward Points with every eligible transaction. These points can subsequently be used to purchase Samsung products or redeem vouchers available through the Samsung Members application, adding further value to everyday payments. As part of the partnership, Samsung and Maybank are also offering exclusive rewards worth up to RM500,000 through a limited-time promotional campaign running from 28 July to 30 October 2026. Eligible customers will receive RM5 after successfully connecting and activating QR Payment on Samsung Wallet, with the opportunity to enjoy up to RM15 in cashback or vouchers when they make qualifying purchases. The launch represents another milestone in Samsung’s efforts to expand Samsung Wallet beyond its existing capabilities and strengthen its role as a comprehensive digital platform for Galaxy users. By bringing together Samsung’s mobile ecosystem and Maybank’s digital banking infrastructure, the partnership aims to provide millions of customers with a more connected, convenient and efficient payment experience.

title: 'Maybank Supports Digital Learning At SMK Santubong | Sarawak Tribune
body: 'KUCHING: SMK Santubong received four Smart TVs from Maybank Sarawak to support digital learning and enhance teaching and learning at the school. The contribution was made in conjunction with Maybank Group’s 14th Global Corporate Responsibility (CR) Day 2026 and Cahaya Kasih Challenge 2026-2027 programme held at the school today. Santubong Member of Parliament, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the initiative was in line with the changing needs of education, particularly as technology continued to play a greater role in learning. She said such support was especially important for schools located away from urban centres, where students could benefit from greater access to digital learning facilities. “This event is to ensure that students are able to gain the knowledge they need through education. Especially for schools far from the city, they really need education like this,” she said. Nancy emphasised that education remained a key priority as it could open pathways to employment, improve incomes, and help families build better lives. “Do not let your place of residence or family backgrounds become a barrier. I believe that with knowledge and continuous effort, all of you can achieve the aspirations you dream of,” she said. Nancy said the collaboration between Maybank and the Santubong parliamentary constituency was not new, with the bank having previously supported Pusat Aktiviti Kanak-Kanak (PAKK) Bandar Baru Samariang in 2024 and 2025. Maybank Sarawak’s Regional Director, Abang Jamili Abang Julai, said the initiative reflected the bank’s role in contributing to the community through education and knowledge-sharing. “This is our opportunity in the banking sector to contribute to the children in school. We hope to share our knowledge in financial literacy, business planning and digital technology to help the community,” he said. More than 60 Maybank employees from its regional office, branches and centres in Sarawak took part in the programme, which also featured sharing sessions on financial literacy and scam awareness. The initiative, guided by the theme ‘Impacting Society Positively: Enabling Well-being For All’, focuses on education, community empowerment and environmental sustainability.

The initiative, guided by the theme ‘Impacting Society Positively: Enabling Well-being For All’, focuses on education, community empowerment and environmental sustainability.

title: 'Maybank Championship makes stellar return, returns with prize bonanza
body: 'THE Maybank Championship is set for another star-studded chapter when Asia’s premier ladies’ golf event returns to Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC) from Oct 29 to Nov 1. With a $3 million (RM12.3m) prize purse, the fourth edition brings together Major champions, LPGA Tour winners and Southeast Asia’s emerging talents for four days of world-class competition at KLGCC. The competition for the coveted Tiger Trophy has never been more intense. Defending champion and Major winner Miyu Yamashita of Japan is one of the most in-form players this season, highlighted by a dominant nine-stroke victory at the CPKC Women’s Open in Canada in August, and a playoff win at the Sony JLPGA Championship in Japan in September. Having claimed a dramatic three-way playoff victory at last year’s Maybank Championship, she will have every intention of becoming the tournament’s first repeat champion. Crowd favourite and World No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand is also on a rich vein of form, having already claimed three LPGA Tour victories in 2026 to take her total title tally to ten. She returns for a fourth consecutive year in pursuit of the elusive Tiger Trophy, having narrowly missed out in each of her last appearances. Thitikul’s close friend Ruoning Yin of China, the 2024 Maybank Championship winner and a Major champion, will also return to Malaysia in winning mode having triumphed at the FM Championship in August. The spotlight will also firmly be turned on Korean ace Haeran Ryu, who is currently second on the LPGA Tour’s Race to CME Globe ranking on the back of successive Major victories in 2026 at the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship and the Amundi Evian Championship. Adding her considerable star power to the field is the perennially popular New Zealander Lydia Ko, a three-time Major winner and reigning Olympic champion who was inducted into the LPGA Hall of Fame in 2024 at age 27. Australian stalwart Hannah Green and Hye-Jin Choi of South Korea, who were the two other protagonists in last year’s playoff, will return with unfinished business on their agendas. The 2023 Maybank Championship winner Céline Boutier of France, who edged Thitikul in a nail-biting nine-hole playoff at KLGCC three years ago, is also in the field. Other fan favourites who have signed up include emerging English sensation Lottie Woad and her experienced compatriot Charley Hull, and Japanese twins Aki and Chizzy Iwai. The Maybank Championship is more than Asia’s premier golf event. It provides a distinctive regional pathway for Southeast Asian talent to earn their place alongside the world’s best. This year, five players who earned their places through the Maybank Championship Asean Qualifier bring that story to life. Held in August at KLGCC’s West Course, the 36-hole qualifier concluded with Thai professional Pimnipa Panthong and her amateur compatriots Sarisa Pojanalai and Achiraya Sriwong locked together at four-under-par 140. Standout Thai amateur Marisa Tojai, who had already claimed four amateur titles in 2026 before arriving at the qualifier, secured the fourth spot at two-under 142, while Malaysia’s Liyana Durisic rounded out the top five at one-under 143. Through this performance-based pathway, each of these five players earned the right to play alongside the world’s best in a full-fledged LPGA Tour event, which is the primary objective of the Maybank Championship Asean Qualifier. For Malaysian fans, there will be plenty to roar about. Liyana Durisic is currently in great form, having already claimed four PGM Tour titles in 2026, and the Women’s World Sand Greens Championship held in Australia in March. She will be joined by a talented and recognizable group of Malaysian players entering as Sponsor’s Invitations, namely Mirabel Ting, Jeneath Wong, Natasha Oon and Kelly Tan, to make up a five-strong Malaysian challenge. 2025 Annika Award winner Mirabel Ting made headlines in 2024 by becoming the highest-finishing Malaysian in Maybank Championship history, with a T12 finish as an amateur. Her fine performances continued into her debut season on this year’s Epson Tour, helping her clinch two victories in 2026. The wins propelled Ting to the top of the Epson Tour’s Race for the Card standings and secured her place on the LPGA Tour for the 2027 season. Joining Ting is Malaysia’s highest-ranked amateur (currently ranked 59th), Jeneath Wong. After a stellar season in 2023 that saw her earn her a major championship start at the US Women’s Open, Wong made history as the first Malaysian to win the Women’s Amateur Asia-Pacific Championship in 2025. The victory earned her further major championship starts, bringing an increasingly impressive international resume to KLGCC. One-time Epson Tour winner and 2023 Epson Tour Rookie of the Year Natasha Oon makes her first appearance at the Maybank Championship since 2023, seeking to capitalize on her encouraging performance at the recent CPKC Women’s Open. The LPGA Tour rookie is rebuilding her momentum following a lengthy injury that saw her miss most of the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Completing the Malaysian line-up is two-time Olympian Kelly Tan, Malaysia’s most successful LPGA Tour player. Tan recorded her career-best results on the LPGA Tour with runner-up finishes at the Dow Great Lakes Bay Invitational in 2022 and 2023, and returns to KLGCC for the third time, bringing over a decade of elite professional experience and an intimate knowledge of the West Course. The Maybank Championship reflects Maybank’s belief in Harnessing Collective Power, bringing together world-class players, emerging ASEAN talent, partners and fans to elevate the game and create opportunity across the region.

title: '2026 Mazda CX-5 – third-gen secures over 600 bookings before launch; Maybank reports circa RM160k price tag
body: 'According to a market insight report by Maybank Investment Bank, Bermaz Auto has secured over 600 bookings for the third-generation Mazda CX-5 ahead of the SUV’s launch on October 8 this year. Bermaz Motor, the official distributor of Mazda vehicles here, previously said the latest CX-5 will initially arrive as a fully-imported (CBU) model before local assembly (CKD) starts “about 12-16 months” later. Estimated pricing for the SUV is said to be from RM170k. In its report, the investment back states that CKD production of the CX-5 will start in mid-2027, with pricing below said estimate at circa RM160k. The report also revealed a new B-segment SUV arriving in either 2027 or 2028, likely priced at around RM120k. This likely points towards the second-generation CX-3, which was confirmed by Mazda last month. As per the Japanese carmaker’s mid-year financial report, the next generation of the CX-3 will be introduced in phases in ASEAN, Japan and other markets from 2027, with Thailand being the production base for the model. Both the current CX-3 and Mazda 2 – the latter sharing the same underlying vehicle platform – have already been dropped from Bermaz Motor’s line-up.

title: 'Selepas 25 Tahun Perkongsian – Maybank Kini Miliki Etiqa Sepenuhnya
body:
'

Maybank kini mengambil alih sepenuhnya Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd selepas membeli baki 30.95% kepentingan dalam syarikat berkenaan. Pengambilalihan ini menjadikan syarikat induk yang memayungi jenama insurans dan takaful terkemuka, Etiqa – kini berstatus anak syarikat milik penuh Maybank secara keseluruhan.

Langkah strategik ini dimeterai menerusi perjanjian pembelian saham bersama Ageas Insurance International NV pada 8 September lalu selepas 25 tahun laksana perkongsian strategik. Dengan pemilikan penuh ini, Maybank berhasrat untuk mengukuhkan lagi kedudukan Etiqa di Malaysia dan Singapura, di samping memperluas pasaran perkhidmatannya ke seluruh rantau Asia Tenggara.

Pengambilalihan ini memberi kelebihan besar kepada Etiqa untuk mempercepatkan inovasi produk, memperluas penawaran takaful, serta meningkatkan kecekapan operasinya. Malah, integrasi terus bersama pangkalan data dan ekosistem perbankan Maybank membolehkan Etiqa menawarkan perkhidmatan yang lebih lancar dan menyeluruh kepada pelanggan.

title: 'Maybank Completes Acquisition Of Remaining Stake In MAHB From Ageas
body: 'Malayan Banking announced that it has completed the proposed acquisition of the remaining 30.95% interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad (MAHB) after signing a share purchase agreement with Ageas Insurance International NV on 8 September 2026.  This follows regulatory approvals from Bank Negara Malaysia that were received on 1 September 2026 for the Proposed Acquisition. MAHB is the holding company for the Etiqa business in Malaysia and Singapore, providing a full range of life and general conventional insurance products as well as family and general takaful products through multi-channel distribution.  President and Group CEO of Maybank, Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, said “With MAHB being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa’s position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank’s customer base. Our focus will be unlocking further value for our customers across Southeast Asia via our regional wealth propositions through cross-selling and delivering more integrated and personalised financial solutions. It will also enhance sustainable and resilient long-term value creation for Maybank with improved capital management within the MAHB group, hence facilitating more effective capital management at the Maybank group level.”  Moving forward, the full ownership provides Maybank and MAHB with greater agility to accelerate product innovation, deepen bancassurance penetration and expand takaful propositions while enhancing capital and operational efficiency across the Group,” added Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli.

title: 'Maybank ungguli Anugerah IR Bursa Malaysia 2026 dengan empat pengiktirafan
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, 7 September 2026 – Bursa Malaysia Berhad mengiktiraf kecemerlangan amalan perhubungan pelabur (IR) menerusi penganjuran Anugerah IR Bursa Malaysia 2026, yang diadakan buat julung kalinya bagi menggalakkan peningkatan standard ketelusan dan komunikasi pasaran modal dalam kalangan syarikat tersenarai awam (PLC). Majlis anugerah berkenaan menyaksikan penyampaian pengiktirafan kepada 32 pemenang merangkumi lapan kategori utama. Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) dinobatkan sebagai Syarikat Terbaik dalam IR (Keseluruhan), selain memenangi kategori Pelaporan Kewangan Terbaik serta Syarikat Terbaik dalam IR bagi Sektor Perkhidmatan Kewangan Kategori Permodalan Besar. Presiden dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Maybank, Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, pula dinamakan sebagai CEO Terbaik dalam IR. Menyampaikan ucaptama pada majlis berkenaan, Ketua Setiausaha Perbendaharaan, Kementerian Kewangan, Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican, menegaskan bahawa komunikasi yang terbuka dan konsisten oleh PLC merupakan antara pemacu utama penciptaan nilai jangka panjang serta daya saing pasaran. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Bursa Malaysia, Dato’ Fad’l Mohamed, berkata dapatan kajian Bursa Malaysia menunjukkan hanya 32 peratus PLC mempunyai fungsi IR dalaman khusus, manakala 17 peratus menggunakan perkhidmatan pihak luar dan 51 peratus lagi masih belum mempunyai struktur IR yang rasmi. “Apabila jangkaan syarikat, pasaran dan pelabur menjadi semakin matang, perhubungan pelabur yang berkesan melangkaui sekadar menyampaikan prestasi kewangan. Ia membantu pelabur memahami kedudukan strategik syarikat untuk masa hadapan,” katanya. Antara pemenang utama lain termasuk Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) bagi kategori Komunikasi Kelestarian Terbaik, Malkit Singh Maan daripada Hong Leong Bank Berhad bagi kategori CFO Terbaik dalam IR, serta Oriental Kopi Holdings Berhad bagi kategori Syarikat IPO Terbaik dalam IR. Penilaian pemenang dilaksanakan menerusi pendekatan berasaskan pasaran yang melibatkan pelabur serta penganalisis tempatan dan antarabangsa. Akses Malaysia merupakan satu saluran pengetahuan dan informasi yang disediakan bagi membolehkan pembaca mendapatkankan info-info terkini dalam dan luar negara.

title: 'Maybank Kini Perkenal Saving+, Bolehkan Pengguna Melabur Serendah RM10 – Menerusi MAE
body:
'

Bagi memastikan pengguna dapat menjana potensi pulangan daripada lebihan tunai tanpa perlu menggunakan platform atau aplikasi pelaburan lain – Maybank kini perkenalkan Saving+ pada aplikasi MAE yang membolehkan pengguna melabur serendah RM10. 

Menariknya menerusi ciri Saving+ ini pengguna boleh melabur dalam dana pasaran wang patuh syariah yang diuruskan oleh Maybank Asset Management. Berdasarkan pengenalan itu, tawaran potensi pulangan dilaraskan sehingga 3.32% setahun.

Di bawah ciri ini juga dijelaskan tiada tempoh penguncian dikenakan bagi tindakan pelaburan dan pengeluaran dapat diproses dalam tempoh purata 2 hari bekerja.

Namun seperti kebanyakkan pelaburan, potensi pulangan kekal tidak dijamin dan tertakluk kepada persekitaran pasaran serta prestasi dana. Dengan pengenalan ciri tersebut, ia sekali gus melengkapkan kitaran MAE – tidak hanya membolehkan pengguna miliki akaun, laksana simpanan tetapi turut merancakkan lagi segmen pelaburan pada pasaran semasa.

title: 'Maybank Matches Up To RM250 In ASNB Units
body: '7th September 2026 - 3 min read Maybank and Amanah Saham Nasional Berhad (ASNB) are running the ASNB Invest & Win Campaign 2026, letting eligible customers who invest in ASNB funds stand a chance to win ASNB units worth up to RM250. The campaign runs from 1 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, split into five monthly phases. To earn an entry, you’ll need to make at least two ASNB investments, in any fund, within the same phase. There’s no cap on the number of entries you can earn. To stand a chance at the full RM250, your total investment within that phase needs to reach at least RM250. If your total is lower, the prize you could win matches that lower amount instead. Each phase draws 148 winners, adding up to 740 across the whole campaign. Each customer can only win once during the entire campaign period, even if they qualify for multiple entries. Bumiputera winners receive Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) units, or ASB 2 or ASB 3 Didik units if their ASB limit has been reached. Non-Bumiputera winners receive Amanah Saham Nasional Equity 5 or Amanah Saham Nasional Sukuk units, depending on fund availability. If a winner has reached the investment limit across all applicable funds, they’ll receive cashback of the same value instead. Winners are selected through a randomiser system on Maybank’s data platform, with witnesses present to verify the process. Only investments made through the MAE app or Maybank2u website count toward this campaign. Investments made at Maybank branches or through the standalone myASNB app don’t qualify, even though they’re valid ways to invest in ASNB. You can start investing in ASNB funds from as low as RM10 on the MAE app (download via Apple or Google Play) or visit Maybank2u. Via the MAE app: Via Maybank2u: There’s no fixed lock-in period, though redemptions are subject to standard settlement timelines. Winning units are credited within 90 days after the campaign ends, and your ASNB account needs to remain active, not dormant or closed, for the prize to be paid out. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates. Iman writes about personal finance with curiosity. She is interested in the stories behind money, the hesitation around big decisions, and the small habits that shape financial futures. 'Maybank Matches Up To RM250 In ASNB Units

'7th September 2026 - 3 min read Maybank and Amanah Saham Nasional Berhad (ASNB) are running the ASNB Invest & Win Campaign 2026, letting eligible customers who invest in ASNB funds stand a chance to win ASNB units worth up to RM250. The campaign runs from 1 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, split into five monthly phases. To earn an entry, you’ll need to make at least two ASNB investments, in any fund, within the same phase. There’s no cap on the number of entries you can earn. To stand a chance at the full RM250, your total investment within that phase needs to reach at least RM250. If your total is lower, the prize you could win matches that lower amount instead. Each phase draws 148 winners, adding up to 740 across the whole campaign. Each customer can only win once during the entire campaign period, even if they qualify for multiple entries. Bumiputera winners receive Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) units, or ASB 2 or ASB 3 Didik units if their ASB limit has been reached. Non-Bumiputera winners receive Amanah Saham Nasional Equity 5 or Amanah Saham Nasional Sukuk units, depending on fund availability. If a winner has reached the investment limit across all applicable funds, they’ll receive cashback of the same value instead. Winners are selected through a randomiser system on Maybank’s data platform, with witnesses present to verify the process. Only investments made through the MAE app or Maybank2u website count toward this campaign. Investments made at Maybank branches or through the standalone myASNB app don’t qualify, even though they’re valid ways to invest in ASNB. You can start investing in ASNB funds from as low as RM10 on the MAE app (download via Apple or Google Play) or visit Maybank2u. Via the MAE app: Via Maybank2u: There’s no fixed lock-in period, though redemptions are subject to standard settlement timelines. title: 'Felda’s Road Ahead in the Spotlight
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Seven years after Malaysians were made aware of the problems confronting the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), the institution is once again at a crossroads. Felda, which has the largest plantation footprint in the country and has helped improve the livelihoods of more than 100,000 original settlers and their families, is undergoing another strategic review amid concerns over its long-term sustainability. An interim report on the Felda Group Strategic Roadmap 2025-2030 (HTF 30) was submitted last month by the Special Committee on the Strategic Plan for Felda Group to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Among the proposals under consideration is a redefinition of Felda’s mandate, including a review of the Land Development Act that governs the agency, as the committee monitors actions taken following the 2019 Felda White Paper, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The review comes as the highly indebted entity grapples with crucial replanting costs that could reach RM900 million annually, on top of more than RM900 million in financing costs currently borne by the government. Felda oversees some 870,000ha of land, of which 490,000ha was allocated to settlers, 330,000ha to Felda’s commercial plantations — later placed under FGV Holdings Bhd — and another 50,000ha for village development. Fragmented and ineffective management of the land and operations, together with questionable transactions and investments, resulted in heavy losses despite Felda receiving billions of ringgit from the listing of its commercial arm, then known as Felda Global Ventures Holdings Bhd. By 2017, Felda’s borrowings had ballooned to RM12.1 billion from just RM100 million in 2007. In 2023, the government guaranteed and agreed to service Felda’s RM9.9 billion sukuk, issued to fund the RM3.7 billion privatisation of FGV to consolidate its estate operations, as well as Felda and settlers’ debt. But more needs to be done before those efforts bear fruit. In 2012, Felda raised RM6 billion through the offer for sale of FGV shares during the latter’s initial public offering, while FGV itself raised RM4.5 billion from investors. In total, the exercise raised RM10.5 billion. Instead of directing more of those proceeds towards critical needs such as replanting, the 2019 Felda White Paper found that RM4.6 billion, or 76% of Felda’s IPO proceeds, went towards what it described as “unproductive spending”, while another RM1.4 billion was channelled into investments that failed to generate returns. The spending included RM1.69 billion in special payments to settlers, RM550 million in one-off contributions to state governments, RM400 million in loans for settlers’ house extensions, RM406 million to redeem FGV shares and RM177 million in listing expenses. FGV, meanwhile, spent RM3.3 billion, or 73% of its RM4.5 billion in IPO proceeds, on investments and developments that did not generate satisfactory returns. FGV, which leased Felda’s plantation land, also failed to achieve the yields Felda had projected, leaving the agency with an earnings shortfall. Following FGV’s privatisation, Felda is looking at consolidating the management of its commercial estates and settlers’ land. But that alone will not resolve the underlying balance-sheet problem, particularly the heavy capital requirements needed to keep the estates productive. Beyond its plantation operations, Felda bears significant social obligations to settlers, including spending on housing, infrastructure and income support for up to five years during the replanting cycle. Today, the families of Felda settlers span as many as six generations and number about 2.8 million people. In many respects, Felda has fulfilled its original mandate of opening up rural land and developing communities alongside settlers, about 95% of whom have received titles to their land. Without a clear framework for its future model, the institution’s role and the financial obligations that come with it risk continuing to be shaped by factors beyond its core mandate, particularly when political considerations intersect with policy during periods of adjustment. Any new roadmap will therefore have to define more clearly where Felda’s commercial responsibilities end and its social obligations begin, and how each should be funded. Felda was in better shape before the mismanagement that followed the windfall from FGV’s listing, when the institution was earning around RM3 billion a year. There are also arguments that greater provisions should have been made for replanting, which is central to sustaining its core operations. Poor investment decisions, however, turned Felda’s fortunes upside down in less than a decade. A forensic audit found RM2.2 billion in asset impairments from eight transactions undertaken by Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) between 2010 and 2018 — equivalent to half of their initial RM4.4 billion investment value. Among them were PT Eagle High Plantations Tbk, the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project and several London properties. One of the largest was Felda’s US$505.4 million acquisition of a 37% non-controlling stake in Eagle High Plantations in 2016 at a premium, resulting in an impairment loss of RM1.576 billion in 2017. Its London property purchases also came under scrutiny over discrepancies between reported acquisition prices and amounts received by vendors, while some properties saw their values fall sharply soon after acquisition. KLVC, meanwhile, remains the subject of a legal dispute between Felda and developer Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd (SPSB) over the development of Felda land along Jalan Semarak. Former FIC chief executive officer Mohd Zaid Abdul Jalil has also been charged with two counts of cheating the company’s board, which allegedly resulted in the ownership of 16 land parcels being transferred from Felda to SPSB. Source: TheEdge - 6 Oct 2026

title: 'The socialist tinge running through Malay society and politics
body: 'By Murray Hunter A CONSISTENT thread of light, humanitarian socialism, the social-democratic and developmental variety, has long run through Malay society and politics in Malaysia. It appears in traditional cultural traits, interpretations of Islamic social ethics, the policies of major Malay parties including UMNO and PAS, and the structure of the modern economy. This form of socialism today is focused on mutual help, social justice, state intervention for equity, and protection of the community, especially the Malay majority. Private ownership, markets and individual enterprise remain, but they operate within a framework of collective responsibility and guided redistribution, through both the New Economic Policy (NEP) and reserved Malay land. Several deep-rooted Malay cultural traits help explain why such ideas found fertile ground throughout Malaya’s contemporary history. Almost forgotten traditions in the traditional kampong, gotong royong was a practical expression of communal cooperation. Villagers regularly came together to build or repair houses, plant and harvest rice, clear drains and paths, maintain the surau or cemetery, and assist with weddings, funerals and other life-cycle events. The familiar proverb “berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing” captured the expectation that burdens should be shared. More broadly, Malay society has tended to favour communalism rather than strong individualism. Group harmony, collective responsibility, loyalty to kin and community, and the avoidance of open confrontation often take precedence over assertive personal autonomy or pure self-interest. This cultural orientation creates a natural affinity for policies that stress mutual support, shared welfare and the idea that the community’s well-being is more important than unchecked individual gain. This is partly explained by Malaysia’s high power-distance score on widely used cultural dimensions such as those developed by Geert Hofstede. In high power-distance societies, hierarchy is accepted as normal, and people are generally more willing to follow authority without extensive public questioning. Among many Malays, this has historically translated into relatively high deference to traditional leaders, the state, religious figures and those in positions of formal power. When government programmes are presented as serving the uplift of the Malay community, this readiness to accept direction from above has made large-scale state intervention more readily accepted than it might be in strongly individualistic, low power-distance cultures. The combination of communalism and hierarchical acceptance helped legitimise ambitious top-down social and economic programmes. Islamic teachings have reinforced the same outlook for many. Obligatory zakat functions as a structured redistribution of wealth from those with surplus to the poor, the needy, debtors and other designated categories. The duty to care for orphans, widows and the vulnerable, the prohibition of riba (usury), and the repeated Qur’anic emphasis on adl (justice) have been interpreted by some Muslim thinkers as containing important socialist elements. Early PAS leader Burhanuddin al-Helmy explicitly combined Islamist, nationalist and socialist ideas in the struggle against colonialism and inequality. Malaysian sociologist Syed Hussein Alatas, in his work Islam and Socialism, argued that Islam’s principles of anti-exploitation and social justice made it compatible with non-Marxist forms of socialism focused on fairness and community welfare rather than atheistic materialism or the abolition of private property. In formal politics, the pattern is clear. Early Malay leftist and populist groups drew on ideas of uplifting ordinary people (marhaen). Within UMNO, the decisive shift came after the 1969 racial riots under Tun Abdul Razak. Razak, who had been exposed to British Labour Party and Fabian socialist thought during his studies, spoke of a form of “nationalist socialism” suited to a developing multi-ethnic nation. The New Economic Policy (NEP) that followed introduced large-scale state intervention with two main prongs: the eradication of poverty regardless of race, and the restructuring of society so that Malays and other Bumiputera could participate more fully in the modern economy and no longer be identified primarily with subsistence agriculture. This was deliberate social engineering aimed at equity and national unity. Key institutions created or expanded in the Razak era still shape Malaysia today. FELDA (Federal Land Development Authority) organised large-scale land settlement schemes that moved hundreds of thousands of rural Malay families onto new agricultural plots, complete with housing, infrastructure, technical support and a structured pathway out of poverty. It was a classic state-led redistributive and developmental programme. MARA (Majlis Amanah Rakyat) was established to advance Bumiputera participation in education, skills training, business and entrepreneurship through scholarships, loans, commercial ventures and institutional support. Together with other agencies, these bodies embodied the belief that the state had a positive duty to correct economic imbalances and uplift the Malay community through organised collective effort. There was an assumption that those privileged leaders would always take the interests of the people into action. PAS has contributed its own version of this tinge. Although primarily an Islamist party, it has at various times emphasised welfare provision, rural development, anti-elite rhetoric and social justice framed through Islamic ethics. In the states it has governed for long periods, PAS has pursued policies with clear redistributive and protective elements that appeal to lower-income and rural Malays who value collective support and moral economy over pure market outcomes. That is partly the reason PAS has been in government there for a long period of time. Today’s economy is reflective of this history The contemporary Malaysian economy continues to reflect the Razak-era model and retains strong features of a light socialist or developmentalist system. Government-linked companies (GLCs) play a dominant role in strategic sectors. The public bureaucracy remains large and central in directing economic activity, allocating resources and implementing preferential policies. Equity ownership targets, subsidies, public education and housing programmes, and extensive state involvement in the economy persist. FELDA and MARA continue to operate alongside a wider network of agencies dedicated to Bumiputera economic advancement. Markets and private enterprise function, freehold land ownership is secure, and individual initiative is encouraged, yet they operate within a framework of heavy government guidance and redistributive goals aimed at social and ethnic equity. This is a mixed economy with a pronounced interventionist and welfare character. The Malaysian economy is not laissez-faire capitalism, nor is it Soviet-style central planning. The focus has always been practical and humanitarian, aimed at reducing poverty, correcting historical imbalances, fostering mutual support, and using the state as an instrument of community uplift. Cultural communalism, acceptance of hierarchy, Islamic ethics of justice, and the institutional legacy of Tun Razak’s era have all sustained this approach. The light socialist colouring remains one of the quieter but durable features of Malay society and politics. It can be traced from the kampong practices of gotong royong and communalism, through the cultural readiness to accept authoritative direction for the common good, the ethical teachings of Islam on justice and redistribution, the ambitious nation-building of Tun Razak’s time with institutions such as FELDA and MARA, and the continuing role of GLCs and state guidance in today’s economy. Unfortunately, many politicians today appear to have forgotten this deeper aspect of the Malay political psyche. Too often they have become focused primarily upon their own personal wellbeing, status and material advancement rather than the broader communal and redistributive responsibilities that once animated Malay political culture. When the ethic of shared burden and collective uplift is neglected in favour of private gain, the original spirit that helped shape both society and policy risks being hollowed out. Recovering an awareness of that older communal and humanitarian strand may be necessary if Malay politics is to remain connected to the values that long gave it meaning. – September 4, 2026
